title: handoff-css config
description: Every house policy handoff-css applies. Nothing in src/ carries a default for these: a consumer states them here, or the generator refuses to run.

name.description: The export's own `schema` field. Any other value is a hard failure.

versions.description: Every `schemaVersion` this consumer has read and vendored. A superseded schema usually still parses, so it is rejected rather than accepted silently.

styles.description: The style-class stylesheet (P21, schema 12+). Optional: an export that publishes no `cssClass` writes no file, and a consumer that names no path never receives one.

handAuthored.description: The consumer's own stylesheet, which wins the cascade (P2).

exclusions.description: EXCLUDED + PRIVATE name lists, for a downstream conformance checker.

paths.description: `"<collection>/<variable>"` prefixes never emitted, regardless of hidden state, and never revived by reachability (P7).

format.description: How an 8-digit hex renders: `#rrggbb` at full alpha else `rgb(r g b / pct)`, or the export's hex verbatim.

motion.description: P19 — MOTION. An EASING variable renders from the export's own curve (`cubic-bezier(…)`, `linear` for a LINEAR curve) and needs no house policy.

timingUnit.description: The unit a TIMING variable (`motion/duration/*`, `motion/delay/*`) publishes. Figma stores seconds. `ms` republishes them as milliseconds, so a step the operator named for its milliseconds reads in the unit its name states (ruling 2026-09-12 row 2); `s` is the pre-0.4.0 form.

delayAliasOf.description: Ruling 2026-09-12 row 4 makes every delay step an ALIAS of the duration step of the same value, so the two can never drift. Naming the two groups lets the generator REPORT a delay Figma authored as its own literal copy (`DELAY_NOT_ALIASED`). It never rewrites one: pairing them here would look identical today and silently overwrite the first delay that legitimately differs. `null` switches the check off.

duration.description: `"<collection>/<variable>"` prefix of the duration ramp it aliases.

aspect.description: P20 — ASPECT RATIOS. Figma has no aspect-ratio TYPE, so a design system authors each ratio as a STRING variable holding `a:b`. This states which variables those are, so they render as the CSS ratio `a / b` instead of a quoted string.

ratioPaths.description: `"<collection>/<variable>"` prefixes whose STRING variables hold a ratio (`core/aspect/`). Their values render as `a / b`; a value that is neither `a:b` nor `a/b` is a hard failure, never emitted as a quoted string. Empty derives nothing and leaves every STRING quoted.

descriptionGroup.description: OPTIONAL cross-check only, never a source of values. The `"<collection>/<variable>"` prefix of the per-column-span HEIGHT groups that encode the same ratios in their descriptions (`layout/grid/aspect/`) — normally also in `exclude.paths`. A leaf group whose descriptions contradict the authored `ratioPaths` variable of the same name raises `ASPECT_DESCRIPTION_DISAGREES`. `null` skips the check.

descriptionPattern.description: A JavaScript regular-expression source matched against those descriptions, whose first two capture groups are the ratio's antecedent and consequent.

collection.description: The collection whose modes are responsive breakpoints, not themes (P3).

variantAttribute.description: The attribute selecting a non-default layout variant.

baseMode.description: Which mode seeds the unconditional base. `collection-default` is the superseded, non-mobile-first rule (P6).

collectionModeAttribute.description: Template for a multi-mode collection with no width or theme semantics. `{collection}` is the slugified collection name.

collection.description: Fallback gate: the collection whose modes are themes if the export publishes no `isTheme` flag (P9.1).

total.description: Theme mode names that replace their siblings entirely, so a nested sibling class cannot re-point tokens under them (P10).

collection.description: The export collection that populates it; null means reset-only.

group.description: The token-name segment the namespace claims and therefore cuts off the leaf (P8.1).

from.description: Populate from `breakpoints.entries` instead of a collection (P8.4).

note.description: Emitted as a comment above the namespace, and shown in the report.

held.description: `[namespace, why]` pairs deliberately NOT reset, each with its blocker stated (P8.3).

rootFontSizePx.description: px -> rem divisor for breakpoints. null reads the export's own `units.policy.rootFontSizePx`.

honourClasses.description: Which responsive classes may change what is emitted (P11). `mode-stepped` and `sample-only` ARE the per-mode default path, so listing them changes nothing; the other four collapse a variable's per-mode samples. An empty list pins pre-0.2.0 output exactly.

heightUnit.description: The unit a `viewport-height` fraction is emitted in, e.g. `dvh`.

widthUnit.description: The unit a `viewport-width` fraction is emitted in, e.g. `vw`.

descriptionFallback.description: Read the `"N% of screen height|width"` description convention as a viewport signal (P11).

groups.description: Variable-name prefixes the consumer declares viewport-relative. A WHITELIST: only these variables may be emitted in viewport units, whatever the export states — a stated fraction outside every prefix keeps its per-mode samples and is reported as `VIEWPORT_OUTSIDE_GROUPS`. A member matching a prefix with neither a `responsive` field nor a matching description also stays px, reported as `VIEWPORT_UNFLAGGED`. An empty list opts out of the gate entirely.

viewport.description: P11 — how a viewport fraction becomes CSS.

aliases.description: P12 — `"<name pattern>": "<target pattern>"`, each ending in exactly one `*`, expanded over the emitted token leaves into a `:root` alias block. A collision with a generated or hand-authored name is a hard failure.

allowNames.description: P16 — custom-property names the consumer legitimately declares outside the export (`--font-suisse`: this package asks consumers to supply their own font face). An allowed name never raises `UNKNOWN_NAME`. It is not a mute button: a name declared in the consumer's own stylesheet is still `LOCAL_ONLY`.

conform.description: P16 — the conformance check's policy. Optional: a config that omits it allows nothing, which is the pre-0.3.1 behaviour.

policyRef.description: Where the consumer's human-readable policy write-up lives.

namePrefix.description: The scale §1 spot-checks against the hand-authored file.

notes.description: House narrative, interpolated into the report with `{{name}}` placeholders. Every key is optional; an absent one leaves its paragraph empty.

regenerateCommand.description: Printed into every generated file, so a reader knows how to reproduce it.
